bands.title: Fewer narcissistic traits
bands.summary: Your answers show relatively few narcissistic tendencies. You may tend to put others' needs and views alongside, or ahead of, your own.

bands.title: Some narcissistic traits
bands.summary: Your answers show a mix. Like most people, you have some narcissistic tendencies alongside empathy and modesty.

bands.title: More narcissistic traits
bands.summary: Your answers show several narcissistic tendencies, such as a strong wish for recognition or sensitivity to criticism. Reflecting on how these affect your relationships can be valuable.

support.text: If these patterns cause difficulties in your relationships or work, a therapist can help you explore them without judgement.

self_importance.low: You tend to see yourself as one among equals.
self_importance.moderate: You have healthy confidence in your abilities, with some sense of being special.
self_importance.high: You often see yourself as more talented or special than others.
self_importance.reflect: How do you feel when others are recognised for their talents?
self_importance.tip: Notice a strength in someone you work or live with, and tell them about it.

admiration.low: You don't depend much on praise to feel good.
admiration.moderate: Praise matters to you, as it does to most people.
admiration.high: Admiration and praise strongly affect how you feel about yourself.
admiration.reflect: How do you feel on days when no one notices what you do?
admiration.tip: Try acknowledging your own efforts privately, without waiting for others to.

attention.low: You are comfortable letting others take the spotlight.
attention.moderate: You enjoy attention at times but don't need it.
attention.high: You enjoy, and often seek, being the centre of attention.
attention.reflect: How much space do others get in your conversations?
attention.tip: In your next conversation, ask two follow-up questions before sharing your own story.

entitlement.moderate: You sometimes feel you deserve more than you get.
entitlement.high: You often feel you deserve special treatment or favours.
entitlement.reflect: When did you last feel something was owed to you, and why?
entitlement.tip: Practise noticing what others give you, and thank them for it.

criticism.low: You can take criticism calmly and learn from it.
criticism.moderate: Criticism sometimes stings, but you usually recover.
criticism.high: Criticism and disagreement tend to hit hard and stay with you.
criticism.reflect: What feedback has stung the most, and was any of it useful?
criticism.tip: When criticised, pause before responding and look for one useful point.

empathy.low: You may find it harder to tune in to, or prioritise, other people's feelings.
empathy.moderate: You care about others' feelings, though not equally in every situation.
empathy.high: You are tuned in to others' feelings and make time for them.
empathy.reflect: When did you last truly understand how someone else felt?
empathy.tip: Ask someone how they are really doing, and listen without steering the conversation.

competition.low: Winning and comparing matter little to you.
competition.high: Winning and outperforming others matter a lot to you.
competition.reflect: How do you feel when someone close to you succeeds?
competition.tip: Try celebrating someone else's success wholeheartedly this week.

recognition.low: You are content even when your work goes unnoticed.
recognition.moderate: Getting credit matters to you, as it does to most people.
recognition.high: Being recognised and credited is very important to you.
recognition.reflect: What would change if no one ever knew about your achievements?
recognition.tip: Do one kind or useful thing this week without telling anyone.

suggestions: Everyone has some narcissistic traits. In balance, confidence and ambition can be strengths.
Noticing how your traits affect other people is a powerful step in self-awareness.
This reflection cannot assess Narcissistic Personality Disorder.
note: Each trait is the average of its 5 answers (reverse-worded questions flipped) on a 0–100 scale. The overall score averages the eight traits, counting Empathy in reverse (more empathy lowers the score). These are MindCheck self-reflection questions and are not validated.
